project.name: exo
project.description: exo connects all your devices into an AI cluster, enabling distributed inference of frontier LLMs (and image models) across multiple devices. It uses MLX as the inference backend with automatic device discovery, topology-aware tensor parallelism, RDMA-over-Thunderbolt support, and OpenAI/Claude/Ollama-compatible APIs.

tour.title: Project Overview
tour.description: Start with the README to understand exo's purpose: connecting all your devices into an AI cluster to run frontier models locally with MLX, automatic device discovery, and RDMA-over-Thunderbolt support.

tour.title: Application Entry Point
tour.description: The Node entry point bootstraps all cluster components — Router, Worker, Master, Election, and API — in a single process. main.py wires them together via dependency injection.

tour.title: Shared Foundation: Events & State
tour.description: exo uses event sourcing for cluster state. The typed event/command/state models in shared/types define the immutable contracts, while apply() is the pure function that folds events into new state.

tour.title: Messaging & Routing
tour.description: The routing layer (zenoh pub/sub) is the backbone of inter-node communication. topics.py defines typed topics (GLOBAL_EVENTS, LOCAL_EVENTS, COMMANDS, ELECTION_MESSAGES), while the event router and router manage the pub/sub plumbing.

tour.title: Master: Coordination & Placement
tour.description: The master coordinates cluster state, indexes events, and places model instances across nodes. placement_utils.py and placement.py implement topology-aware auto-parallel placement decisions.

tour.title: Worker: MLX Inference Engine
tour.description: Workers handle inference tasks and manage runner processes. The MLX engine drives tensor-parallel generation, with the runner supervising model processes and the coordinator orchestrating downloads.

tour.title: Model Download & Management
tour.description: The download coordinator fetches model weights from HuggingFace with rate-limit handling and directory management, ensuring models are available before inference starts.

tour.title: API Layer: OpenAI-Compatible Server
tour.description: FastAPI server exposing OpenAI Chat Completions, Claude Messages, Responses, and Ollama-compatible APIs. Adapters translate between API request shapes and internal text-generation types.

tour.title: Dashboard: Svelte Frontend
tour.description: The Svelte 5 + TypeScript dashboard provides cluster management and chat UI. The main route and layout mount the app, with lib/components holding chat and model-selection components.

tour.title: Rust Networking Core
tour.description: Rust provides high-performance zenoh networking (gossipsub, peer discovery) exposed to Python via PyO3 bindings in exo_rs, plus system-level operations like pidfile management.

tour.title: Testing & Integration
tour.description: The test suite spans integration tests (1, 2, and 4-node clusters), dashboard tests, and resilience tests, built on the shared test framework and conftest fixtures.

tour.title: Model Download Flow
tour.description: The download coordinator manages fetching model weights from HuggingFace with rate-limit handling, directory management, and progress tracking before inference can begin.

tour.title: Event Sourcing Deep Dive
tour.description: exo uses event sourcing for cluster state management. Events are typed discriminated unions; apply() is a pure function that folds events into immutable state snapshots.

tour.title: Benchmarking Infrastructure
tour.description: The bench/ directory contains performance evaluation tools including prefill/decode benchmarks, parallel request testing, and scenario-based evaluation configs.

tour.title: iOS/macOS Client App
tour.description: The Swift app provides a native client interface for the exo cluster, communicating with the Python API server via HTTP. Includes cluster state models and UI components.

tour.title: Build System & Reproducibility
tour.description: The Nix flake defines reproducible build environments for all components (Python, Rust, dashboard), with Apple SDK overlays and Metal toolchain configuration.
